title: Slate a take for a phone camera: clapperboard square to the lens and in frame, one fast clap with the board kept still
instruction: Slate the take: clap the clapperboard shut once, with it facing the phone camera and fully in its picture.
context: Slating is the clapperboard snap that starts a take on film sets and, increasingly, on phone shoots: the frame where the sticks meet is lined up with the clap's sound. Camera assistants hold the slate with one hand and close the clapper with the other, and the slate must not move while the clapper is in motion. Here the 5 mm acrylic board leans back 40 deg on a box and cannot stand by itself, and its hinge's tension screw holds the stick wherever it is left, so the stick must be driven shut.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Acrylic film clapperboard (Neewer acrylic director's clapboard, 30 x 25 cm), loose, 0.50 kg: black acrylic writing board 30.0 x 20.0 x 0.5 cm printed with white field lines; fixed lower clapstick 30.0 x 2.5 x 0.8 cm along its top edge; upper clapstick (same size, white with black diagonal stripes) on a hinge pin through both sticks 1.2 cm in from the board's end on the robot's right (the camera's left), free end on the robot's left; the stick opens 0 to 50 deg and the hinge's tension screw holds it at any angle. Sticks shut, the board stands on its bottom edge with the middle of that edge at x 28.4, y 0, writing face toward the phone (+x), leaning back 40 deg from vertical with its back on the box's far top edge. (2) Corrugated cardboard box (SimReady box_cardboard_d01), loose, 1.5 kg, 26.4 (x) x 34.5 (y) x 16.6 cm tall, x -12.4 to 14.0, centred on y 0. (3) Phone (iPhone 15 size, 14.8 x 7.2 x 0.8 cm) in landscape in a clamp on a tabletop tripod, fixed: main camera lens at x 72, y 0, 13 cm up, looking straight back along -x; 26 mm-equivalent lens filming 16:9 (69.4 x 42.6 deg field of view) at 240 fps. (4) Yellow tape strip 22 x 4.8 cm on the table along the camera's axis, x 40 to 62, y 0. Distractors, loose, ignored by scoring: (5) paper coffee cup (SimReady food_beverage_coffeeCup_a01), 8.5 cm across, 11.7 cm tall, 0.25 kg, at x 52, y 31; (6) roll of tape (SimReady tape_clear_a01), 0.12 kg, at x 66, y 22; (7) notebook (SimReady misc_notebook_a01), 22.9 x 17.0 x 1.0 cm, 0.12 kg, at x 53, y -30, turned 23 deg. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read at 240 Hz (every physics step; a real trial uses 240 fps video): the stick's opening angle and the board's pose. A clap: the stick reaching 0.5 deg or less (sticks meeting) after it was opened 15 deg or more. The first clap is the take's sync mark and is the one judged. 0: no clap; or at the first clap the board's face is more than 20 deg off the line from its centre to the lens, or any of its four outer corners is outside the phone's 69.4 x 42.6 deg picture. 0.25: the first clap faces the phone and is in its picture. 0.5: and it is fast: at most 12 frames at 240 fps (50 ms) from the last frame with the stick 10 deg or more open to the first frame shut. 0.75: and the board is still: its face centre stays within a 1 cm range over the 60 frames (0.25 s) before and the 60 after the clap. 1.0 (success): and for the 1 s after the clap the stick never opens 5 deg or more again (no bounce, no second clap) and the board stays facing the phone and in its picture. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Shut the stick and lean the board on the box's far top edge as in the screenshot: its bottom edge on the tape marks at x 28.4, leaning back 40 deg (its top edge 19.2 cm up). Check the box is on its marks, the phone is in its clamp at the marked height and is recording slow motion at 240 fps, and the arms are at the ready pose. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the board and sticks are boxes, the hinge a joint with friction for the tension screw and a joint limit for shut (no stick weight, no bounce, no sound: the clap is read from the hinge angle at 240 Hz). Phone and tripod are fixed primitives; its view is a pinhole check of the board's corners, not a render, and occlusion by the hands is not checked. Box and distractors are SimReady props. Contact friction is the simulator's high default.
